Apply the backward test(s,z)->P_(t-s)f(z) in Dynkin's formula. For fixed t,

No Markov property of Z alone, coefficient derivatives, switching bound,
common invariant law for actual generators or frozen-rate replacement
is used in this identity.

For a countable network, obtain(1) first under finite-population stopping
and bounded tests, then pass to the limit with the growth bounds below.
Elementary channels with positive population increment have at most one
reactant, so bounded multipliers give a linear-birth population comparison.
It supplies all finite-horizon moments needed for localization at any
fixed finite t. Exponential-in-t localization bounds are not used as a
polynomial compiler resource estimate. The uniform bounds below are
